ai.description: Giri's Bronzeback reaches 70–90 cm. It is bronze-brown dorsally with a distinct black lateral stripe and a pale yellow venter. Key features include a prominent black eye-stripe and a bluish-white neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dendrelaphis girii* is best distinguished by its distinct, broad, and continuous black vertebral stripe that extends from the neck onto the tail, unlike similar congeners.
ai.habitat: Dendrelaphis girii inhabits the evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Giri's Bronzeback is a diurnal, arboreal hunter that actively pursues lizards and frogs through the forest canopy with remarkable speed and agility.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis girii* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April to August) in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dendrelaphis girii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
